name: com.manofmany/mcp
title: Man of Many
description: Man of Many's men's lifestyle reviews, buyer's guides, gift ideas and deals. Free, read-only.

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description:
Search Man of Many's published articles, reviews and buyer's guides.

    Use for any question about men's lifestyle where Man of Many's take would help: watches,
    style, grooming, cars, drinks, tech, travel, food, gifts. Returns titles, links, authors,
    dates and short excerpts (not full articles). Buyer's guides rank first.

    Args:
        query: what to look for, e.g. "dive watch under $2000" or "best aftershave".
        category: optional section, e.g. Watches, Style, Cars, Drinks, Tech, Grooming, Travel.
        limit: number of results, 1 to 15 (default 8).

tools.name: get_article
tools.description:
Get the summary of one Man of Many article: standfirst, outline and key picks.

    Returns the article's headline, author, dates, standfirst, section outline and (for
    buyer's guides) the ranked picks. Never the full text: link readers to the url.

    Args:
        url_or_slug: a manofmany.com article URL or its slug, e.g. "dive-watches".

tools.name: latest
tools.description:
Get Man of Many's newest stories, optionally for one section.

    Args:
        category: optional section, e.g. Watches, Cars, Style, Drinks, Tech, Travel, Grooming.
        limit: number of stories, 1 to 20 (default 10).

tools.name: get_buyers_guide
tools.description:
Find the Man of Many buyer's guide for a product type and return its ranked picks.

    Use when someone asks "what's the best X" (dive watch, running shoe, espresso machine,
    cologne, whisky). Returns the best-matching guide with each pick's name, price as
    published, a short verdict and the retailer link exactly as it appears in the article,
    plus other related guides.

    Args:
        topic: the product type, e.g. "dive watches", "white sneakers", "beard trimmer".

tools.name: product_picks
tools.description:
Shortlist products Man of Many recommends, across its published guides and gift guides.

    Use for gift ideas and shopping questions, e.g. "gift for a coffee lover under $200",
    "watch under $1,500". Each pick comes with the guide it is from, our short verdict, the
    price as published and the retailer link exactly as published.

    Args:
        query: the product, recipient or interest, e.g. "gifts for dads who cook".
        max_price_aud: optional budget ceiling in AUD; picks without a listed price are dropped.
        limit: number of picks, 1 to 20 (default 10).

tools.name: gift_finder
tools.description:
Gift ideas from Man of Many's published gift guides.

    Args:
        recipient: who it is for, e.g. "dad", "boyfriend", "groomsmen", "coffee lover".
        budget_aud: optional maximum spend per gift in AUD.
        interests: optional interests, e.g. "golf, whisky".
        limit: number of ideas, 1 to 20 (default 10).

tools.name: deals
tools.description:
Current sales, discount codes and Man of Many's deal roundups (Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Christmas).

    Use when someone asks about sales, deals, discount codes or where to buy for less. Returns Man of
    Many's recent deal articles plus live offers and coupon codes from its Australian retail partners.

    Args:
        query: optional product or retailer, e.g. "headphones", "Apple", "The Iconic".
        limit: number of articles, 1 to 15 (default 10).

tools.name: mci_overview
tools.description:
About the Man of Many Male Confidence Index 2025 (MCI): what it is, method, sample, how the
    index is scored, caveats and links. Call first before using the other mci_* tools.

tools.name: mci_questions
tools.description:
List Male Confidence Index 2025 survey questions: id, wording, answer options and who answered
    (men, women or everyone). Use the id with mci_results or mci_rows.

    Args:
        search: optional words to filter on, e.g. "support", "social media", "income", "relationship".

tools.name: mci_results
tools.description:
Weighted results for one Male Confidence Index 2025 question, optionally split by a demographic.

    Returns weighted percentages (single choice and multi-select) or weighted means (numeric), with the
    unweighted n for each cell. Cells under 30 respondents return suppressed: true.

    Args:
        question_id: e.g. "Q15", "Q11" (multi-select group), "F9", "D9". See mci_questions.
        by: optional split, e.g. "age_group", "state", "income", "gender", "employment", or any single-choice id.
        gender: optional "men", "women" or "all" (default: whoever answered the question).
        filter: optional {variable: value} to restrict the base, e.g. {"age_group": "18-28"} or
            {"S2_age": "30-39"}; use "a|b" for several values.

tools.name: mci_scores
tools.description:
Weighted Male Confidence Index (0-100) and the five domain scores (each 0-20) for Australian men,
    optionally split by a demographic (age_group, state, region, income, education, employment,
    household, housing, sexuality, or a single-choice question id such as Q15).

    Args:
        domain: optional one of finances_career, health_wellbeing, relationships, cultural_identity,
            self_perception_direction (default: index plus all domains).
        by: optional split variable.

tools.name: mci_rows
tools.description:
Anonymised respondent-level rows from the Male Confidence Index 2025, for your own analysis.

    Each row has row_id, the requested columns and Weight (always use it). Page with offset and
    next_offset. Rows are anonymised (no identifiers, shuffled, free text redacted).

    Args:
        columns: variable ids or question groups, e.g. ["S1", "age_group", "Q11", "Male_Confidence_Index"].
            Default: gender, age, state, index and domain scores.
        filter: optional {variable: value}, e.g. {"gender": "Male", "state": "Victoria"}.
        offset: start row (default 0).
        limit: rows per page, 1 to 200 (default 50); pages are capped at about 60kB.
        labels: true for answer labels (default), false for numeric codes (smaller; see mci_questions).
